rows: Why is getting to LEO so expensive?
~9.4 km/s of ΔV required (gravity losses + drag + need for orbital velocity); the rocket equation means most of the rocket is propellant
What is LEO vs GEO vs HEO?
Low Earth Orbit (200-2000 km); Geostationary Earth Orbit (35,786 km, synchronous); High Earth Orbit (>35,786 km)
What was the first milestone of the "new space" era?
SpaceX Falcon 9 first-stage booster landing, December 2015 — proving orbital-class booster reuse was practical
Effective exhaust velocity ÷ g₀ = efficiency metric for rockets; higher Isp = more efficient use of propellant; chemical ~300-450 s; electric ~1500-10,000 s
Ended US dependence on Soyuz for ISS crew transport; first crewed orbital commercial flight (SpaceX Dragon) in 2020; established model for NASA as customer
